title: Canonical local ideal products and sheafified ring and module quotients
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with topology $J$, let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal subsheaf [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-ideal]. For an $R$-module sheaf $F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], call a restriction-stable family $N(U)\subseteq F(U)$ of submodules locally saturated if membership in $N$ can be checked on covering sieves. Define $IF$ as the intersection of all locally saturated submodule families containing $I(U)F(U)$ for every $U$, where $I(U)F(U)$ is the submodule of finite sums of ideal multiples. Define the quotient module presheaf as the sectionwise cokernel of $IF\hookrightarrow F$, and $Q_I(F)$ as its module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], with projection $q_{I,F}$ the cokernel projection followed by the sheafification unit. Define the quotient ring presheaf by $U\mapsto R(U)/I(U)$ with induced restrictions, its sheafification $S_I=R/I$, and $\pi_I:R\to S_I$ the quotient projection followed by the sheafification unit. For $I'\subseteq I$, define $t:S_{I'}\to S_I$ by sheafifying the sectionwise quotient maps. Regard $S_I$ as an $R$-module by restriction along $\pi_I$, and define $F\otimes_R S_I$ using the existing sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].
